name: Keyboard layout map
plain: Which character each physical key produces, revealing QWERTY, AZERTY, QWERTZ, Dvorak etc.
meaning: Tells native keyboard layout and so likely country and language (French AZERTY, German QWERTZ, Colemak enthusiasts). Chromium returns about 48 key codes, no prompt.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell your keyboard layout, such as QWERTY, AZERTY or QWERTZ
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page or app loads
can: Check which letter each physical key types, about 48 keys
Guess your country and language from the layout
cannot: Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.differs: Only Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: The page can tell whether your keyboard is QWERTY, AZERTY or something else.
story.for_you: You may see correct keys shown in a game or editor. You do not see that the site learned your layout. No prompt appears.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to place game keys and shortcuts well. Trackers use it to guess your country and language and to tell you apart from others.

use_cases.example: A browser game shows 'Z Q S D' as movement keys for a French player.
A music web app maps its piano keys to your physical key rows.
A web editor shows the right shortcut hints for your layout.
A fingerprinting script adds the layout to a device profile.
A fraud tool flags a mismatch between layout and the claimed country.
An ad profile guesses language from an uncommon layout when other signals are missing.

history.change: Shipped, top-level frames and permissions-policy keyboard-map gated
